messages:
sam.k: Heads up — noticed a streaming tail latency regression on canary after the kernel-selector change. P95 for medium sequences jumped ~120ms -> ~280ms. Repro steps and quick notes below.

remy: Oof. Any flamegraphs or perf output? where's the hot path?

sam.k: Quick summary from a short repro run: `replay_harness --trace=prod-2026-03-15.json --streaming=on --chunk-size=128 --concurrency=40 --seed=20260315`
```
# perf top snapshot (aggregated)
  sel_kernel_v2                38.7%  (gpu kernel selection/hotpath)
  allgather_copy               22.1%  (GPU memcpy / small copies)
  client_readloop_poll         11.3%  (serial read loop stalls)
  kv_cache_lookup              6.4%   (higher misses than baseline)
```

sam.k: Flame shows a big triangle from sel_kernel_v2 -> allgather_copy -> client_readloop_poll. Looks like kernel selection favored larger micro-batches that increased memcpy pressure and triggered backpressure in the read loop.

tina: That matches my hunch — if chunk sizes get bigger we push more tokens per GPU op and the transport (grpc/http chunking) can't keep up, so the client readloop queues up and P99 spikes. Also saw KV cache misses higher after selector change?

sam.k: Yes — kv-hit ratio dropped ~3.5 percentage points on the canary run. I suspect the selector is picking a quantized kernel variant that bypasses a fast-path cache layout.

kai: Can we do an apples-to-apples run: same model binary, same seed, same trace, toggle only the selector flag? I want deterministic comparison. Use the replay harness with warmup and fixed rng. Example: `./replay_harness --trace=prod-2026-03-15.json --streaming=on --chunk-size=128 --seed=42 --warmup=2000 --collect=perf,kvstats,readloop`

olivia: I ran a micro synthetic test with wrk to compare streaming vs non-streaming: `wrk -t8 -c120 -d30s http://localhost:8080/v1/generate?stream=true` -> throughput same, but streaming P99 latency jumped 2.4x. Non-streaming P99 stable.

remy: Good. Two hypothesis to test: 1) kernel selector chooses larger kernel -> more memcpy/allgather 2) batching heuristic changes batch alignment with KV cache causing extra misses -> more work overall. Both amplify client readloop backpressure.

perf-bot: Canary rollback initiated for service=runtime-canary at 2026-03-17T15:12:30Z — reason: streaming-p99-regression > threshold (:exclamation:).

sam.k: Proposed plan (short):
- Step A: Reproduce deterministically with replay harness (kai + sam) using seed=42 and collect perf maps + pprof.
- Step B: Instrument KV cache counters (hits, misses, evictions, avg-ttl) and compare baseline vs selector-on.
- Step C: Run microbench for client readloop variants (read sizes 64/128/256, non-blocking vs blocking) to see stall behavior.
- Step D: If selector is root, add a quick fallback: if kv-hit_rate drops >2% or memcpy time >20% increase, pick alternate kernel.

kai: I'll spin up the replay run now and attach output. Starting command: `./replay_harness --trace=prod-2026-03-15.json --streaming=on --chunk-size=128 --seed=42 --warmup=2000 --duration=60 --collect=perf,kvstats,readloop`

olivia: For readloop tests I have a small harness that simulates slow transport: `python tools/sim_readloop.py --delay-ms 5 --max-chunk=128` — I can run combos and dump CSVs.

remy: Also add an apples-to-apples non-streaming baseline with identical kernel-selection off (force `--kernel=baseline`) to ensure we isolate streaming-specific behavior.

sam.k: Thanks. Action items: kai/replay + perf maps, olivia/readloop sims, tina/kv counters, remy/compare kernels. We'll reconvene once we have perf flamegraphs + kvstats CSV. :thumbsup:
